analysis:
Examined the BASE release/signing/recovery guidance at docs/operations/provider-release.md:482–770 and HEAD:1–481 against the canonical asset/boundary index and supplied TB-002/TB-011 details. The visible HEAD change is the update date (line 3); surrounding guidance preserves explicit release approval, trusted-source checks, environment-scoped publication credentials, permanent revocation and the distinction between official artifact identity and serving authorization (HEAD:104–131, 270–292). Shared signing identity, APNs collisions, model weights and fan-helper interactions are unchanged context, not new findings.
The bounded patch adds final-archive cluster runtime facts before payload preparation (HEAD hunk:577–579) and indicates new registration fields. BASE:623–642 establishes that cluster helpers were already packaged, signed and verified, so their existence alone is not new attack surface. However, the new payload text and added HEAD:649–795 are outside these source excerpts. Integration must inspect those additions and corresponding generation/publication consumers to establish whether facts are informational or affect runtime admission, how they bind final helper/Metal bytes, and whether release credentials can alter qualification or revocation behavior (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054, TB-011). No concrete regression is supported by the examined units; missing implementation and added documentation remain coverage limits, not evidence of safety.
